title: Bedmap3 updated ice bed, surface and thickness gridded datasets for Antarctica

nodes.title: Background & Summary
nodes.summary: Describes Bedmap3, an updated gridded dataset suite for Antarctica (south of 60°S) covering surface elevation, ice thickness, and seafloor/subglacial bed elevation. It adds 84 new aero-geophysical surveys (52 million points, 1.9 million line-km) from 15 providers, filling gaps in East Antarctica, mountains, coastlines and the Peninsula. Also presents an updated Bedmap3/RINGS grounding line, ice shelf thickness, rock outcrops and bathymetry. Data-driven method without ice sheet models; ice volume (27.17 million km3) and sea-level potential (58 m) similar to earlier Bedmaps; reveals subglacial landscape in greater detail.

nodes.title: Methods
Geoid, projection, and grid cell size.
nodes.summary: Describes the Bedmap3 methods: a classification mask and grids of surface elevation, ice thickness, bed topography and uncertainty, built from interpolated survey data (airborne and ground ice thickness, ship bathymetry), satellite-derived rock outcrop, surface and ice shelf data, and grounding zone features. Uses geoid gl04c, EPSG:3031 projection, and 500 m grid spacing versus Bedmap2's 1 km. Notes survey sampling is anisotropic and 93% of ice thickness cells are interpolated.

nodes.title: Masks of grounded ice, transient grounded ice, floating ice shelf and rock.
nodes.summary: Describes Bedmap3's revised grounded/floating ice limits, produced with SCAR Antarctic RINGS. Previous grounding-line mappings (altimetry, InSAR, optical) are spatially discontinuous and inconsistent. The grounding line was derived from InSAR, altimetry, imagery and multi-source products, using a tidal heat map and modal line for 2018, plus Landsat 8 coastline and ice-shelf limits (Jan-Mar 2022). A new 'transient grounded' class marks ice shelf areas that ground only at low tide, validated against a 2024 pinning-point study (95% agreement). Mask classes are grounded ice, transient grounded ice, floating ice shelf, and rock, with cell counts.

nodes.title: Ice thickness data and gridding.
Filtering and weighting of survey data.
nodes.summary: Describes Bedmap3 ice thickness data processing: 82 million raw survey points from 277 surveys over 60 years were summarised into 4.13 million points and gridded at 500 m. Overlapping surveys differ due to navigation, analogue versus digital sounding, picking algorithms and pulse repetition rate. Cell values are a count-weighted mean favouring recent dense surveys; rock and zero-over-ice points are excluded, and single-point cells in the Amundsen Sea Embayment are dropped. About 8% of points were filtered, yielding 3.15 million cell values. Also covers the reconciled grounding line (Fig. 3, Table 1 sources) and mean survey years (2006.9 overall).

nodes.title: Ice shelf thickness.
nodes.summary: Describes Bedmap3 ice shelf thickness processing: an updated CryoSat-2 freeboard grid (2011–2014, 92.3% coverage) is used, with freeboard-derived thickness excluded within 3 km of the grounding line due to hydrostatic equilibrium limits. Survey data (447,327 points) calibrate spatial biases, excluding marine-ice-affected radar data on FRIS and Amery, using seismic data for FRIS. Median-filtered, spline-interpolated 500 m calibration grids are subtracted, yielding a mean thickness of 468 m (SD 244 m). Table 2 gives survey point mean years for selected areas.

nodes.title: Synthetic ice thickness data: Glen’s flow law for ‘thin ice’.
nodes.summary: Describes Bedmap3 ice thickness methods: synthetic thin-ice thicknesses near rock outcrops from Glen's flow law (using flow speed, slope, temperature, firn air content), calibrated to 84,984 radar surveys (scaled by 1.44). Covers synthetic grounded coastal margin thicknesses based on surface height and flow speed, trough 'streamline' interpolation guided by survey alignments, and Topo-to-Raster gridding of all data sources into a continuous ice thickness grid.

nodes.title: Synthetic ice thickness constraints and trough streamlines for Antarctic Bedmap3 interpolation
key_items: Synthetic ice thickness data: grounded coastal margins.
nodes.summary: Describes synthetic ice thickness points for unsurveyed grounded coastal margins, derived from surface height and flow speed (factors of 9, 2, and 1 by flow class), giving 13,378 points with mean 70 m. Also covers 'streamlines': nearly 5000 manually defined along-trough segments linking topographic lows between survey profiles, used with Topo to Raster linear interpolation to represent subglacial troughs, improving on Bedmap2 and complementing mass-continuity methods like BedMachine.

nodes.title: Interpolation of the ice thickness grid.
key_items: Synthetic ice thickness data: grounded coastal margins
nodes.summary: Describes how an ice thickness grid is interpolated from survey data points, derived ice shelf thickness, synthetic thicknesses (Glen's flow law, grounded margins, streamlines) and rock outcrops using the Topo-to-Raster algorithm with specified gridding options. Explains the adapted thin plate spline method, which fits curved surfaces while minimising curvature, producing smooth transitions across data gaps including grounded ice to ice shelf, with linear interpolation along trough long profiles. Also covers Fig. 4 showing freeboard-based ice shelf thickness calibration on the Ross Ice Shelf using survey measurement biases, median filtering, spline interpolation and bias correction.

Bedmap3 ice thickness and gridding: 82 million raw survey points (277 surveys) summarised to 4.13 million and gridded at 500 m, using count-weighted means with exclusions and filtering (about 8%). Covers the reconciled grounding line, ice shelf thickness from CryoSat-2 freeboard calibrated to survey data, synthetic thin-ice and coastal thicknesses via Glen's flow law, trough streamlines, and Topo-to-Raster thin plate spline interpolation.

nodes.title: Surface elevation.
nodes.summary: Describes the surface elevation dataset for Antarctica: a gap-filled REMA Digital Elevation Model (Gapless-REMA100, ~1 m accuracy, 100 m grid, 2007-2017 imagery) resampled to the 500 m Bedmap3 grid and referenced to mean sea level via the g104c geoid. Covers manual removal of coastal elevation spikes and lows, gap filling at shifted ice shelf fronts, median filtering, and setting non-positive elevations to +1 m. Also includes ice thickness data sources (survey, freeboard-derived, synthetic Glen flow law, coastal margin, streamline points) and Ellsworth Mountains thickness validation.

nodes.title: Bed topography.
nodes.summary: Describes Bedmap3 construction: bed topography derived by subtracting ice thickness from surface elevation, with rock outcrops and Lake Vostok water column handled; merging with the IBCSO v2 bathymetry at 500 m spacing, using tidal-based water column constraints and smooth grounding-zone transitions. Covers timestamps (survey years ~2007-2022), comparisons with Bedmap2 and BedMachine v3 (troughs, mass conservation, suggested combined approach), data record grid names and formats, and quality-control checks on masks, elevations, thickness and discontinuities.

nodes.title: Bedmap3 Coastal Merging, Timestamps, and Comparison to Earlier Products
key_items: Comparison to earlier Bedmap products and BedMachine v3.
nodes.summary: Describes how the grounded bed and coastal bathymetry were merged iteratively, cropping and interpolating a 10 km coastal gap and enforcing positive water column thicknesses using FES2014 tidal ranges. Notes Bedmap3 components date from about 2007-2022, with thickness survey mean year 2006.9 and regional surveys more recent. Compares Bedmap3 with Bedmap2 and BedMachine v3: Bedmap3 shows more defined troughs and smoother grounding-zone transitions, while BedMachine better captures fast-flow troughs; combining both is suggested.

Bedmap3 methods: a classification mask and 500 m EPSG:3031 grids (surface elevation, ice thickness, bed topography, uncertainty) built from interpolated survey, satellite, and ship data, with 93% of thickness cells interpolated. Grounding line and masks (grounded, transient grounded, floating shelf, rock) were revised using InSAR, altimetry, and Landsat 8, validated at 95% agreement. Covers thickness gridding, REMA-based surface elevation, bed topography merged with IBCSO v2, tidal coastal merging, and timestamps (~2007-2022). Compared with Bedmap2 and BedMachine v3, combining both is suggested.

nodes.title: Data Records
nodes.summary: Describes a 500 m gridded dataset (13334 x 13334, 16-bit signed integer, -9999 no-data, metres) available at a DOI in TIFF and NetCDF formats. Grids cover surface, thickness, bed, masks, bed and thickness uncertainty, and survey data point counts (bm3 prefix). A point shapefile of linearly interpolated streamline thicknesses (bm3_streamlines_pt) is also provided.

nodes.title: Technical Validation
Quality control checks.
key_items: Comparison to earlier Bedmap products and BedMachine v3.; Data Records
Comparison to earlier Bedmap products and BedMachine v3.
nodes.summary: Bedmap3 technical validation: quality-control checks on grid cells (sea/non-sea bed and surface heights, grounded ice thickness, ice shelf cavity and transient-grounded column rules, rock cells, grid alignment, integer data type, mask category agreement with imagery, no discontinuities in thickness or bed, flotation check for coastal grounded ice). Also Figure 8 compares Bedmap3 bed to Bedmap2 and BedMachine v3. Table 5 statistically compares Bedmap1, Bedmap2, BedMachine v3 and Bedmap3 on areas, volumes, mean and thickest ice, bed elevations, deepest points, and sea-level equivalent.

nodes.title: Uncertainty estimates.
Surface DEM uncertainty.
nodes.summary: Describes uncertainty estimates for the Bedmap3 Antarctic grids, based on error budgets combining published uncertainties and internal accuracy/precision tests, given at about 1-sigma. Surface DEM: REMA has near-zero bias and RMSE under ±1 m for most of Antarctica, under ±2.4 m on steep slopes; the gapless 100 m REMA version has ±3 m RMSE and ±4 m absolute accuracy without ground control, giving a combined Bedmap3 surface uncertainty of ±7 m, with local errors possibly up to ±18 m in the Antarctic Peninsula. Fig. 9 compares Bedmap3 and BedMachine v3 beds in the Rutford Ice Stream area, noting Bedmap3's smoother grounding zones and better-resolved bed areas.

nodes.title: Ice thickness uncertainty.
nodes.summary: Describes Bedmap3 ice thickness and bed uncertainty. Individual survey precision is about 5 m IQR from crossovers, per-cell combined uncertainty under 10 m, and about 20 m for single-measurement cells. Synthetic thin-ice thicknesses have IQR 152 m, coastal thickness 15 m, and ice shelves about 10 m. Interpolation error grows logarithmically with distance from data, from 73 m to 272 m. Also covers FRIS radar-seismic differences, Fig. 10-12 bed comparisons with BedMachine v3, and Table 6 summary.

nodes.title: Bed topography uncertainty.
nodes.summary: Describes uncertainty in Antarctic bed elevation and bathymetry for Bedmap3. Grounded bed uncertainty is ±7 m (rock) to ±12 m (surveyed) and ±276 m (interpolated), from combined topography and ice thickness errors. IBCSO v2 bathymetry is about 24% surveyed (±10 m) and 76% interpolated, with shallow biases up to 1000 m and independent regional checks (Nivl, Totten) showing biases of 7–250 m. Interpolated bathymetry uncertainty ranges ±60 m to ±306 m with distance from data. Also includes a code availability statement (no custom code), publication dates, and a long reference list of datasets and studies.

Uncertainty estimates for Bedmap3 Antarctic grids, combining published and internal error budgets at about 1-sigma. Covers surface DEM error (REMA under ±1 m RMSE, ±3 m for gapless 100 m version, combined ±7 m, up to ±18 m in the Peninsula) and Fig. 9 bed comparison with BedMachine v3. Covers ice thickness (survey precision ~5 m IQR, per-cell under 10 m, interpolation error 73–272 m) and FRIS comparisons. Covers bed topography (grounded ±7 to ±276 m; IBCSO v2 bathymetry biases up to 1000 m, regional checks 7–250 m) and code and references.

Technical validation of Bedmap3: quality-control checks on grid cells (bed/surface heights, ice thickness, ice shelf cavities, rock cells, grid alignment, data type, mask agreement, discontinuities, grounded-ice flotation) and comparisons with Bedmap2 and BedMachine v3 (Figure 8, Table 5). Uncertainty estimates (about 1-sigma) for surface DEM, ice thickness, and bed topography, including bathymetry biases, regional checks, and FRIS comparisons.

summary: Bedmap3 is an updated gridded dataset for Antarctica (south of 60°S) covering surface elevation, ice thickness, and bed elevation. It adds 84 new aero-geophysical surveys (52 million points, 1.9 million line-km) from 15 providers, filling gaps in East Antarctica, mountains, coasts, and the Peninsula, plus updated grounding line, ice shelf, rock, and bathymetry data. The data-driven method yields ice volume and sea-level potential similar to earlier Bedmaps. Methods use 500 m grids with masks validated at 95% agreement. Data records are provided as TIFF and NetCDF with a point shapefile. Validation covers quality checks, comparisons with Bedmap2 and BedMachine v3, and uncertainty estimates. Acknowledgements list funders, support, and authors.
